predecessors.name: Yogyakarta Sultanate
predecessors.text: the countryside around Yogyakarta, Mataram, Bagelen and Magelang, where the page puts the main fighting of 1825-1827

successors.name: Dutch East Indies
successors.text: the 'killing area' between the Progo and Bogowonto rivers, where the rebels were confined in 1828-1829 (disc read from the two river names)

ledger.x: July 1825: the war for central Java begins.
July 1827: the rebels lose the Yogyakarta country.
28 March 1830: Diponegoro is arrested at Magelang and the rebellion ends; the remaining rebel land passes to Dutch control.

wars.name: Java War
wars.outcome: Dutch victory: the benteng system confined the rebels (258 forts, 133 built 1828-1829); Kyai Maja surrendered in November 1828, Diponegoro's remnants were defeated at Siluk on 17 September 1829, Sentot surrendered in October 1829 and Diponegoro was arrested…

certainty.note: A guerrilla war: the page names fighting places and a 'killing area' between two rivers, not a front line.
